data.G: Preparation only: retain the baseline. After research closes, integrate the best correctly validated measured candidate, then independently confirm the integrated G; do not assume gains combine.
data.analysis: Choose N=2: the baseline reads A coalesced across threadIdx.x but writes C with lane addresses separated by n, so a coalesced shared-memory tiled transpose is the direct opportunity. A warp-register/shuffle transpose is a distinct alternative that may avoid shared-memory staging and a block barrier; finer tile tuning belongs within the first tree rather than warranting a redundant third tree. The supplied baseline is valid and correct; its three n=1024 samples average 16.919 microseconds (score 0.5). These are baseline search measurements only—there are no child comparisons or independent confirmations yet. The CUDA 12.6.3 Best Practices Guide describes coalesced global accesses and shared-memory transpose staging with padding to avoid bank conflicts. Judge candidates by timed n=1024 performance only after correctness checks for all required sizes, and independently confirm the final integrated program.

children.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Replace the baseline's strided global stores with a single-pass shared-memory tiled transpose: load input rows coalesced, exchange tile orientation in shared memory, then store output rows coalesced. Explore the padded 32x33 tile and useful block-row/CTA mappings or tile variants, measuring the complete run at n=1024. Preserve the run entry point and exact bit patterns; produce every C element for every positive n multiple of 32, pass correctness at n=32, 64, 256, and 1024, use no new allocation or other file edits, and report build, correctness, and repeated timing evidence.
children.subject: Coalesced shared-memory tiled transpose

children.objective: Own only src/candidate.cu. Independently explore a warp-register transpose using warp lane permutations/shuffles to turn coalesced input loads into coalesced output stores, aiming to avoid CTA shared-memory staging and its block-wide synchronization. Tune the warp's element ownership and tile mapping; do not simply reproduce the shared-memory implementation. Preserve exact bitwise copies and the run entry point, produce all output for every positive n multiple of 32, pass the required correctness sizes, allocate no new storage, and report build, correctness, and repeated full-run n=1024 timing evidence.
children.subject: Warp-level register/shuffle transpose
